records.name: validate:atlas-units
records.risk_prevented: Prevents two incompatible quantities from sharing one demand field again. `volume` held monthly search volume on keyword-tool rows and this domain's OWN 90-day impression count on GSC rows, and rank_score was computed straight off it, so 'ai business coach' scored on 5 impressions instead of its real 110/mo search volume - 22x low - and sorted below queries with a fraction of its market demand.

records.overlap_analysis: Does not duplicate VAL-113 (validate:query-atlas), which gates PUBLISHABILITY on evidence tier and cluster coverage. This gates the UNIT CONTRACT: that the ambiguous field is gone, that a GSC row's search_volume carries keyword-tool provenance, that demand_basis matches the populated fields, that rank_score is banded so units never sort as peers, and that no source file still reads the removed field.
records.decision: ADMITTED as HARD_FAIL: rank_score is the input to every page decision, and a unit error there is silent - it produces a plausible number rather than an error. The source-scan check exists because a stale consumer reading the removed key would get null, not a throw.

records.name: validate:admission-level-stability
records.risk_prevented: A build stage silently re-levelling pages that are already in data/content/page_admission_registry.json. admission_level decides which lane contract validate_programmatic_admission.py enforces on a page, so re-levelling at build time either fails the release on a corpus that was never written against those thresholds, or - in the demotion direction, which is the live risk now that 1,466 records carry 'full' - removes published pages from the substantive checks while the build still passes.
records.existing_coverage_gap: validate:programmatic-registry only checks that admission_level is one of baseline/full. validate:programmatic-admission reads the level and reports how many records it is skipping, but treats whatever the build wrote as given. validate:demand-backed-pages warns about pages admitted after the gate that carry "baseline", not about pages whose level the build changed. Nothing compared the committed registry with the built one, so generate_aplayer_phase_expansion.mjs promoting all 1,400 of its pages to "full" on every run was invisible until 2,250 lane-contract errors landed in CI - truncated to the first 300, which read as "300 short pages".
records.overlap_analysis: Does not duplicate validate:programmatic-admission, which judges page bodies against the level recorded for them. This one judges the level itself, and only its stability across a build. It does not overlap validate:clean-rebuild-parity either: that compares two builds of the same tree, so a stage that re-levels deterministically is identical in both and passes.
records.decision: ADMITTED as HARD_FAIL in container-prepush, placed immediately before validate:content-release so a re-levelling is named before the lane-contract failures it causes. The promotion incident that motivated it is resolved at the cause (6a759335d gave the 1,400 generated pages the material to earn 'full'), but nothing keeps that correct: this guard is what makes the next silent re-level - in either direction - fail on its own name instead of as 300 truncated lines of downstream symptoms. Both fixtures are executed by the script on every run, so the recorded proof cannot rot into decoration.

records.name: validate:search-measurement-truthfulness
records.risk_prevented: Prevents the search-measurement lane from reporting zeros while calling itself healthy: an all-zero GSC dataset marked OK, a target-query filter that discards every returned row in silence, URL Inspection verdicts discarded after being paid for, an ingest failure swallowed by `|| true`, and a sitemap lastmod that is either stale or stamped with build time.

records.name: validate:citation-signal-join
records.risk_prevented: Prevents competition_opportunity - a weighted, declared scoring input - from silently measuring nothing while looking like it works. The citation lookup was keyed on a scalar `query` that a cluster record does not have (it carries a nested queries[]), so all 120 clusters recorded "this query has not been probed" while 83 grounded observations sat unused, and the engine correctly dropped the component and redistributed its weight, which made a 100% failure indistinguishable from normal operation. Also prevents "a grounded answer cited nobody of ours" being scored as maximum open ground for a brand or navigational query ("sprylabs", "spry reddit"), and requires the run to disclose how much of the component was actually measured.
records.existing_coverage_gap: validate:scoring-contract checks the shape and range of a score. Nothing checked whether the citation signal reached any scored item at all, whether a navigational query could be scored as open ground, or whether a component that measured nothing said so.
overlap_analysis: VAL-SCORING-CONTRACT covers score shape; this covers whether the measured citation input reaches the score at all and whether it is honest about it.
records.decision: Admitted after query_scores.json showed 0 of 120 clusters with a competition_opportunity reading while data/signals/llm_citation_observations.json held 83 grounded observations, and the scored population and the probed population were found to have zero overlap.

records.name: validate:no-silent-zero-work
records.risk_prevented: Prevents any lane from exiting 0 while having produced no work. Guards the exact defects found in this audit: the zero-dollar citation plan discarding 100% of its candidates behind a permanently-disabled fixture gate while printing PASS; the apply stage hardcoding status PASS with release_units_applied=0; the strategy gap-fill lane queueing 10 candidates a day that no consumer ever turns into files; the answer-surface scorer reading a file nothing writes while the real citation probe wrote elsewhere; the admin dashboard rendering a stalled zero identically to a healthy day; the search-intelligence lane re-observing the same 24 of 120 targets forever; and validate_fanout_warning hardcoding status PASS with 3110 findings.
records.existing_coverage_gap: No validator could tell 'this lane did no work' apart from 'this lane had no work to do'. validate_daily_proof_packet checked field presence and arithmetic but never asserted that a PASS implied work; validate_safe_harbor_autopublish only inspected units that were applied, so applying zero units vacuously passed.
overlap_analysis: VAL-DAILY-PROOF-PACKET checks the proof packet's shape and arithmetic; this checks whether the work it reports actually happened.
VAL-SAFE-HARBOR-AUTOPUBLISH inspects applied units for unsafe claims; it passes vacuously when zero units are applied, which is precisely the state this catches.
records.decision: Admitted after the zero-dollar citation lane was found to have applied zero candidates for 8+ weeks while reporting PASS, and four further lanes were reproduced with the same shape.

records.name: validate:lastmod-ledger-final
records.risk_prevented: Prevents a sitemap lastmod ledger being committed that does not describe the tree it ships with. The ledger was derived part-way through a release, later stages rewrote the pages it had just hashed, and it was committed alongside them: at 6aac79a2e the committed ledger contradicted 1,900 of 2,223 committed pages. Nothing failed where the bad ledger was produced; it surfaced days later as an 8-URL sample mismatch inside sitemap:lastmod:self-test, on branches that had cut from main and inherited the failure as if it were their own. This asserts the committed ledger against every committed page, refuses a freshly derived ledger that already disagrees with the tree, and statically requires every content-release mode to derive the ledger as its final stage.
records.existing_coverage_gap: sitemap:lastmod:check deliberately treats 'the page changed since the ledger was written' as a soft note, because failing the prepush profile on every build that touched a page would make the gate permanently red. sitemap:lastmod:self-test samples 8 URLs and only those whose evidence is git_last_visible_content_change, so 1,900 stale records could reduce to one reported filename. Neither compares the committed ledger to the committed tree, and nothing at all constrained WHERE in a release the ledger was derived.
overlap_analysis: VAL-SEARCH-MEASUREMENT-TRUTHFULNESS runs sitemap:lastmod:check and the self-test; both judge whether a published date is a lie, and both are deliberately soft about a ledger merely being behind. This judges whether the ledger describes the tree it was committed with, which is the condition that makes it become a lie later.
VAL-SITEMAP-COVERAGE checks which URLs are present in a sitemap; it says nothing about whether their lastmod was derived from those pages.
records.decision: Admitted after the ledger at 6aac79a2e was reproduced as stale for 1,900 of 2,223 URLs, having been derived before the release stages that rewrote those pages and committed with them; re-deriving by hand had already cleared the same symptom twice in one day without touching the ordering that produced it.

records.name: validate:ledger-receipt-run-scope
records.risk_prevented: Prevents a lastmod derivation receipt inherited from the commit being read as proof that THIS run derived the ledger. The receipt lives under artifacts/, which the main-writing lanes commit, so from 93977956f (2026-09-03 12:58Z) every checkout began with a receipt already hashing to the ledger beside it. Spry Content Release run 33767079923 never executed sitemap:lastmod:content - full-content-cycle derives the ledger as its last stage and the lane fails at selfheal, the stage before it - yet arm B of validate:lastmod-ledger-final believed a derivation had happened, compared the untouched committed ledger to a working tree the release stages had rewritten, and reported 1590 of 2231 pages stale. Nothing was stale. Self-heal correctly refused to repair it and the scheduled lane paged its owner every day. Both doors are held: ledgerDerivationReceipt refuses a receipt byte-identical to the one at HEAD, which protects every tree that already carries a committed one; .gitignore plus a narrowed staging pathspec in commit_and_push_if_changed.sh stop new ones being committed at all. The staging exclusion is deliberately limited to artifacts/validation/*receipt*.json, because most of that directory IS read across runs - pre-implementation-protected-hashes.json, workflow-yaml-inventory.json, daily-citation-release-plan.json and internal-navigation-structure.json all have readers with no fallback - so a blanket exclusion would freeze inputs and let the release exit 0 having published nothing.
records.existing_coverage_gap: VAL-LASTMOD-DERIVATION-RECEIPT asserts that a receipt is written on every derivation and that a receipt whose hash no longer matches the ledger is refused. It says nothing about WHICH RUN wrote the receipt, and it runs its predicate in a scratch directory that is not a git repository, so the committed-receipt case cannot arise inside it. VAL-SITEMAP-LEDGER-FINAL is the validator that consumes the receipt and so cannot be its own guard.
overlap_analysis: VAL-LASTMOD-DERIVATION-RECEIPT proves a derivation records itself; this proves the record belongs to the run reading it, and carries the negative arm that a page rewritten after a genuine in-run derivation is still a hard failure, so the recurrence cannot be cleared by disabling arm B.
VAL-SITEMAP-LEDGER-FINAL is the subject under test here, driven end to end in throwaway git repositories rather than read as source.

VAL-MAIN-WRITER-VALIDATION-GATE exercises the commit helper's push and dispatch behaviour; this asserts what that helper is allowed to STAGE, by lifting its real git add line out of the script and running it in a throwaway repository.
records.decision: Admitted after Spry Content Release run 33767079923 was reproduced: an inherited receipt made arm B of validate:lastmod-ledger-final report 1590 of 2231 pages stale in a run that had derived nothing, turning the scheduled content lane red every day from 2026-09-03.

records.name: validate:build-cache-integrity
records.risk_prevented: Guards scripts/build/ (the content-hash cache wrapping `npm run build:all`, docs/runbooks/BUILD_CACHE.md). Prevents a cache entry existing for a build that never reached exit 0, an entry with a non-empty diff and no payload to restore, a stale payload sitting next to a claimed empty-diff (fixed-point) entry, and the safety invariants in cached_build_all.sh/save_build_cache.mjs/restore_build_cache.mjs being weakened without a validator noticing. This is the exact class of defect that produced FROZEN_OUTPUT_MATERIAL_SHRINK on 2026-09-01: a snapshot taken from a tree build_navigation_structure.mjs and build:visible-faq had not finished writing to yet.
records.existing_coverage_gap: No validator existed for scripts/build/ before this cache was added in this change; the extraction-surface guard and freeze/shrink guards protect the GENERATED tree, not the cache mechanism sitting in front of build:all that decides whether to regenerate it.
overlap_analysis: VAL-EXTRACTION-SURFACE-GUARD-CHECK verifies the GENERATED tree converged; this verifies the CACHE deciding whether to regenerate it is internally consistent - neither checks the other.
VAL-BUILD-ALL-INTEGRITY (validate:build-all-integrity) checks build:all's own output contract; this checks the wrapper that decides whether build:all runs at all this time.
records.decision: Admitted alongside the build cache itself: a cache that can restore a half-built or failed-build tree is worse than no cache, so the guard shipped in the same change as the mechanism it governs, not after.

records.name: validate:admin-command-verify
records.risk_prevented: Keeps the Admin Command workflow provable without turning it red, and keeps its three copies of the command list in agreement. The workflow's only run ever - 33274444603 on 2026-08-29, event=workflow_dispatch - was an audit dispatching action __parse_probe__ with reason 'audit parse probe'. The workflow was healthy; run_admin_command.mjs threw because __parse_probe__ was not a registered command, so confirming the lane worked is what made it fail, and that failure stayed the latest status of an ACTIVE workflow. There was no green way to probe it: every registered command mutated data/admin/runtime_control.json and was committed to main. This asserts that a read-only command exists, is offered by the dispatch dropdown, exits 0 having actually examined the registered commands and the control state, writes nothing, and is gated out of the commit step; and that the mutating commands still work.
records.existing_coverage_gap: Nothing checked that the workflow could be exercised at all. validate:workflow-write-scopes judges permissions, not reachability. The command list now exists in three places - data/admin/command_registry.json, the dispatch branches in scripts/admin/run_admin_command.mjs, and the choice options plus commit gate in .github/workflows/admin-command.yml - and YAML cannot read JSON, so without this guard they are three lists with no link, which is how the original defect was possible.
overlap_analysis: VAL-WORKFLOW-WRITE-SCOPES checks what a workflow is permitted to write; it says nothing about whether the workflow can be run without changing main.
The admin-command.yml registry record describes the workflow as a state-control surface; it does not assert that its command list matches the script's or the dropdown's.
records.decision: Admitted after run 33274444603 was reproduced as a healthy workflow made permanently red by the only means available for probing it. Carries two negative arms: a registry with no commands must hard-fail (Rule 0), and a registered command whose handler is deleted must hard-fail.

records.name: validate:workflow-manual-only-declared
records.risk_prevented: Admin Operations has never run on main and nothing in the repository could say whether that was deliberate or whether the lane had silently died; 'never ran' looks identical for a workflow nobody needed to dispatch and a workflow everyone forgot. This reconciles every trigger-less workflow against data/workflows/manual_only_workflows.json in both directions, so a manual-only lane must state why it is manual and a declaration that has gone stale fails on the trigger, not on the wording. It also fails a dispatch dropdown that no step gates on and no script reads, which would let every option exit 0 having done nothing the operator asked for.
records.existing_coverage_gap: validate:workflow-contract already resolves npm scripts and node entrypoints for every workflow, so command reachability is deliberately NOT duplicated here. faux_trace_all_workflows.py builds one trace per dispatch option but never asserts the option reaches anything and keeps its own hardcoded copy of the option list. Neither asks whether a workflow with no automatic trigger is intentionally manual, which is the question that had no recorded answer.
records.decision: Admitted to answer, in data a validator reads, whether a workflow that has never run on main is intentionally manual or silently dead.

records.name: validate:repair-fixture-capability
records.risk_prevented: scripts/selfheal/heal_until_clean.mjs registers a repair for ten validation steps and nothing in this repository had ever run one. The map could not even be read without running self-heal, because it was defined inside a module that executes a full validation loop at import time. A repair whose validator is GREEN is exercised by nothing, so its capability can be removed without a single check noticing - until production needs it, at which point self-heal runs the repair, the repair exits 0 having changed nothing relevant, the loop burns its attempt budget and exits UNRESOLVED, and the release lane deadlocks with the ingest half still pushing behind it. The sibling repo local-guides-citation-velocity lost eleven days and accumulated ~690 undelivered recommendations to exactly that. This proves each registered repair still CLEARS a constructed failing state, off the production tree, while its validator is green.
records.existing_coverage_gap: VAL-CITATION-REPAIR-REACH and validate:health-boundary-reach each prove ONE repair is aimed at pages its validator judges, statically; neither runs a repair and neither reads the REPAIRS map. Nothing else in the repository references the map at all. There is no static repair contract, no commit-coverage check and no efficacy check here, so a repair that has gone inert is indistinguishable from one that is simply not needed today.
records.decision: Admitted 2026-09-09 with nine of ten registered pairings proven behaviourally FAIL -> PASS against real failure modes in a throwaway git worktree; measured 97s locally. Proven negatively: re-pointing VAL-VISIBLE-CONTENT-ARTIFACTS at repair:programmatic-registry-owners produced repair_does_not_clear naming the pairing, re-adding the removed VAL-EXTRACTION-CONTRACT-SELF-TEST pairing produced undeclared_repair, and the grow-only floor produced behavioural_coverage_fell; restoring the map returned PASS.
